content.subject: US Has Lost Measles Elimination Status, Researchers Say
content.preview_text: Nvidia investors back a slow CEO search, a Starship first and Zelenskyy on a Donbas vote.
content.description: Researchers say measles is spreading regularly again in the US, plus an Nvidia investor letter, a Starship first and a Donbas question.
content.contents_extra: Israel's strike on a Hamas commander explained, trivia and your poll

stories.title: Researchers Say the US Has Lost Its Measles Elimination Status

photo.alt: A hand holds a syringe and a flu vaccine vial; illustrative file photo.

paragraphs: The United States has lost its measles elimination status, according to researchers with direct knowledge of the decision. NPR reports the Pan American Health Organization concluded measles has reestablished regular transmission in the country. The researchers spoke to KFF Health News.
The U.S. had held the status since 2000. CBS News reports the CDC has tallied 5,412 cases so far in 2026. That is more than double last year's total of 2,242 cases.

The CDC counts at least six measles related deaths this year, and some states report more. CBS News reports Pennsylvania alone has reported more than 1,500 cases and seven deaths associated with the disease this year.

Why it matters. Measles can now spread in ongoing chains among unvaccinated people. CBS News reports PAHO says a vaccination rate of 95% or higher is the best protection. CBS News reports PAHO is set to hold a news conference on Tuesday.

stories.title: Two Big Nvidia Investors Urge the Board to Keep Huang's Return on the Table

photo.alt: An Nvidia GeForce RTX graphics card installed inside a computer; file photo.

paragraphs: Two large Nvidia shareholders asked the chipmaker's board to take its time choosing a new chief executive. CNBC reports Altimeter Capital's Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management's Gavin Baker want the search to leave room for Jensen Huang's return.

Huang resigned Thursday after reports about personal relationships, amid an independent board investigation. The letter did not call for his immediate reinstatement. It said interim chief Colette Kress can capably lead the company.
The two firms disclosed about $2.13 billion of Nvidia stock combined as of June 30. CNBC reports Elon Musk said he signed a petition to reinstate Huang.

Why it matters. Nvidia sits at the center of the artificial intelligence boom. CNBC reports a fund manager says other chip suppliers could fill demand if buyers lose trust in Nvidia. Investor Dan Ives says chip demand still outstrips supply four to one.

stories.title: SpaceX Catches the Upper Stage of Starship for the First Time

photo.alt: A stainless steel rocket stands beside a launch tower; file photo.

paragraphs: SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship rocket with mechanical arms on its launch tower Saturday. CNBC reports it was the first catch of the spacecraft returning from orbit. The catch happened at Starbase, Texas.
The ship orbited Earth 14 times on a 22 hour mission. The Guardian reports the craft descended into the clutch of the tower's arms. BBC News reports SpaceX called the landing picture perfect.
SpaceX diverted the booster on Friday, and it exploded before hitting the Gulf of Mexico. CNBC reports the company also released 26 new Starlink satellites, adding to a constellation of over 11,000.

Why it matters. A reusable Starship could cut launch costs and speed satellite deployment. NASA is counting on Starship to carry astronauts from lunar orbit to the Moon's surface. Flight 15 was the first try at catching both stages.

stories.title: Zelenskyy Says Ukrainians Would Get a Say on Any Donbas for NATO Deal

photo.alt: The Independence Monument column on Maidan Nezalezhnosti in Kyiv; file photo.

paragraphs: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says U.S. negotiators asked whether Ukraine would leave Donbas if it were admitted to NATO. CBS News reports he said it was the first time the question had been raised.
Zelenskyy said Kyiv would not surrender its territory. CBS News reports he said any arrangement would not recognize occupied land as Russian. He also rejected a commitment to neutrality.

He is discussing a security package with NATO and European Union guarantees, troops, weapons and financial support. CBS News reports he said he would ask Ukrainians whether to accept such an exchange. He said he has no right to decide alone.

Why it matters. Control of Donbas has been a recurring sticking point in peace talks. CBS News reports Russian President Vladimir Putin has demanded Ukraine pull its forces out of the region as a precondition for peace. U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said Washington is now facilitating direct engagement between Moscow and European partners.

deep_dive.title: What Israel's Killing of a Hamas Commander Means for the Gaza Truce

photo.alt: A family sits in a makeshift tent among damaged buildings; file photo.

paragraphs: An Israeli airstrike killed the commander of Hamas's Rafah Brigade in southern Gaza on Saturday. BBC News reports Samir Abu Younis was killed in the Al-Mawasi area. Hamas confirmed his death.

What happened. BBC News reports eyewitnesses said four missiles struck a tent in a camp sheltering hundreds of displaced people. Al Jazeera reports the strike wounded two others. Israel's military said it took steps to limit harm to civilians.

The backstory. Hamas's armed wing called Younis one of the most important commanders in planning the Oct. 7, 2023 attack. He had led the brigade since Sept. 15. He took over after the death of the previous commander. Al Jazeera reports Israel had designated Al-Mawasi a humanitarian zone but has struck it repeatedly.

What comes next. A ceasefire took effect on Oct. 11, 2025. Strikes have continued since then. Gaza's Health Ministry says Israeli attacks killed 16 people over 48 hours. It counts at least 1,643 Palestinians killed since the truce began. Cold related deaths have risen to 11, including a baby who died of hypothermia. Most residents, many of them displaced, live in tents or damaged buildings after recent heavy rains. Hamas said Younis's funeral would be held Sunday afternoon in Khan Younis.

trivia.question: Since what year had the United States held measles elimination status?
trivia.explanation: C. 2000. CBS News reports the country was declared measles free that year.

World view: ASEAN leaders open Manila summit. Trump is expected to join a special summit with the bloc on Nov. 17 as oil shortages hit the region; Al Jazeera reports.
Iraq fires nine officials over smuggling. Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi dismissed security officers after a probe found illegal oil refineries; Al Jazeera reports.
Need to know: Airlines expect a full recovery Sunday. More than 900 Sunday flights were canceled as of late Saturday, and the FAA chief saw zero evidence of anything nefarious; ABC News reports.
Saturday cancellations topped 5,000. More than 5,000 flights were canceled Saturday after Friday's nationwide halt, FlightAware data show; CBS News reports.
Money & markets: Canadian stocks gain since the midterms. The TSX is up 1.6% since the vote as investors bet on softer U.S. trade policy; CNBC reports.
Family offices bet small on startups. Megadeals made up 87.5% of U.S. venture funding in the first half of 2026, but some investors favor younger firms; CNBC reports.
Future frontiers: AI cheating rattles South Korea. The top scorer on a national tax accountant exam confessed to using generative AI, days before the college entrance test; The Guardian reports.
Data center doubts weigh on AI. Dan Ives estimates 10% to 20% of planned data centers may not be built after Democratic gains in Congress; CNBC reports.
The score: US routs Haiti 6-0. Christian Pulisic scored twice in Mauricio Pochettino's penultimate game before the second leg in Cincinnati on Tuesday; The Guardian reports.
Harrison keeps her UFC title. Two time Olympic judo champion Kayla Harrison submitted Amanda Nunes at Madison Square Garden; The Guardian reports.
Life & culture: Bands play for stranded flyers. Simple Plan, Hoobastank and The Used sang their hits over plane PA systems during the travel delays; ABC News reports.
Philippines wins Eurovision Asia. Carmelle, 19, took the first contest in Bangkok with 211 points for her song Sobra-Sobra; BBC News reports.

uncertainties: Measles status loss attributed to researchers with direct knowledge (KFF via NPR/CBS); PAHO formal announcement expected Nov. 17; none found as of ~09:45Z Nov. 15.
Death counts differ: CDC at least six; Pennsylvania reports seven.
Gaza tolls from Gaza Health Ministry via Al Jazeera.
